meanings.note: Drawing attention. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to see', paired with 'увидеть'.

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'Vika', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: Wait, are you not listening to me at all?

meanings.note: For emphasis.

meanings.en: to hear out, listen attentively to
meanings.note: Listen until the end. Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'слушать'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to listen to, hear out', paired with 'выслушивать'.

examples.trans: First listen to me very carefully.
The judge patiently heard out the witness's testimony.

examples.text: Сначала выслушай меня очень внимательно, Аркаша.
examples.trans: First listen to me very carefully, Arkasha.

говорить.gloss: to speak, to say, to talk

emphatic at the start of a sentence

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.

examples.text: Кто здесь снимает? Кто оператор? Запись идёт?

meanings.note: + genitive: 'из мэрии' = from the town hall

meanings.note: + dative. Core Russian prep meaning 'to, towards' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: There's someone here to see you.

meanings.note: A person's own room at work. From French 'cabinet' (private study or office).

examples.trans: Nikolai Filippovich, I'm in the mayor's office right now.

meanings.note: Agreeing, often reluctantly. Core Russian part meaning 'all right, OK' in everyday speech.

meanings.note: + instrumental; между собой = between yourselves/themselves

meanings.note: + prepositional: на сайте. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.

meanings.note: К + dative. Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to come up (to), to approach', paired with 'подходить'.
Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to come up (to), to approach', paired with 'подходить'.

examples.text: Нам не нужна ваша приставка! Ещё раз подойдёте к моему ребёнку — пожалеете!

подходить.gloss: to approach, to come up; to suit

meanings.note: очередь подходит = one's turn is coming up

Это мне подходит = that suits me. Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'ходить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to approach, to come up; to suit', paired with 'подойти'.

examples.trans: Let's go, our turn in the queue is coming up.
The train is approaching the station.

examples.text: Я к печке подхожу. А он маячит перед глазами!
examples.trans: I walk up to the stove. And it dangles right before my eyes!

meanings.note: Informal. Core Russian interj meaning 'bye' in everyday speech.
As an adverb. Core Russian interj meaning 'bye' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: to have a look, to take a look
meanings.note: One completed look. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'смотреть'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to have a look', paired with 'смотреть'.
Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'смотреть'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to have a look', paired with 'смотреть'.

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'appeared in a dream'.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и присниться вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and appeared in a dream on time.

examples.text: На нашей кухне все умеют присниться.

meanings.note: about a feeling or pain: потом пройдёт = it'll pass

просить прощения = to ask for forgiveness

meanings.en: to intend, to plan, to be going to
meanings.note: + infinitive. Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to intend, to be about to; to gather', paired with 'собраться'.

Pack or assemble. Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to intend, to be about to; to gather', paired with 'собраться'.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
